text:
The Rangers have been one of the better teams in the league at creating chances and one of the worst at finishing them. They own 53.2% of expected goals (the quality of chances each side gets) yet have scored about ten fewer goals than those chances predict. At 13-10-1 they are about where their luck has left them, and our numbers give them a 59% shot at the playoffs.

The injuries are the story of the month. Pavel Dorofeyev went on injured reserve, and Yahoo Sports reported two more forwards, Smits and Bjorkstrand, out two to three months. That is why the club went to Vancouver for Max Sasson, and why Glenn Gawdin, who scored his first two NHL goals against the Canucks, has become a name people know. J.T. Miller, meanwhile, has been written up by the New York Post for a resurgent "grind game"; his line with Dorofeyev was winning 64% of the chances before the injury.

Igor Shesterkin is on a heater, .926 with four goals saved above expected over his last four starts. Mika Zibanejad, Alexis Lafrenière and Gabe Perreault have been the steadiest line, and Adam Fox with Vladislav Gavrikov the busiest pair. Mike Sullivan's team plays the right way more nights than not. What we'd watch is whether the depth Sasson and Gawdin provide can hold that process together until the bodies come back.
headline: The Rangers deserve better, and they are banged up
